_about: The one place GenClass plans are defined. telemetry-worker/src/plans.ts imports this file (limits, entitlements, Stripe lookup keys, the billing page) and genclass.dev's site reads it (the pricing page). Three plans since version 3 (2026-11-11): Free, Team and Enterprise. Free is what finds, shows and fixes the problems: the open-source runtime with every mode and its on-device model, the coding-agent loop on the developer's machine, the dashboard's problems for one person (3 apps, the last 7 days shown) and genclass-dev[bot] on public repositories. Team is sold per developer (per_seat true: the Stripe subscription's quantity is the number of seats, one for the account's owner and one for each member; telemetry-worker/src/team.ts) and adds what a team uses: genclass-dev[bot] on private repositories, visitor analytics, forwarding, export, 90 days of history and members. Enterprise is agreed by email: a null monthly price means the plan is not sold on the site, and an account gets it from GenClass's own grant (accounts.comp_until, set by hand to the end of the agreement; accounts.comp_plan names the plan granted, grant_plan when it is empty). The classifier a person from GenClass trains is in Enterprise only. retired_plans lists the plan ids GenClass sold before (Pro and Custom until 2026-10-19, Individual until 2026-10-22): their Stripe products and prices stay GenClass's own, so a subscription to one is still cancelled with its account, opens Manage billing and is reported to the owner while it bills, but it gives no plan (it reads as Free). The worker's Stripe code and scripts/stripe-setup.mjs sell any plan given a monthly price above 0, its stripe_lookup_keys and a stripe_tax_code. Prices are US cents (per seat for a per_seat plan); a null yearly price means no yearly option. limits.apps null means no plan limit (the worker still caps an account at 200 apps against abuse); limits.seats is how many people a plan that is not per_seat holds (null: no limit); limits.history_days is what the dashboard shows, and data is never deleted before 90 days whatever the plan, so the longer history is there the moment an account upgrades. Ingest never depends on the plan: an app's visitor analytics are counted while its plan leaves them out, and shown once it includes them. There is no trial. Feature lines with available false are shown as coming next. The entitlement github_private is what lets genclass-dev[bot], the GitHub App, review an account's private repositories (telemetry-worker/src/github/entitlement.ts); public repositories are reviewed for everyone, whatever this file says. A self-hosted collector sets PLAN_GATES = "open" and gives every account the grant plan. managed_payments true would sell a plan through Stripe Managed Payments (only for fully automated digital products; telemetry-worker/README.md, Paid plans).
